title: Training program for UTMB: interview with David Roche (Andrew Skurka)
population: Coach guidance for athletes recovering from a 100-mile race
findings: A full-throttle 100 'takes around a full month to recover from for most athletes': a week of rest, a week of slow running, a week of slow running plus a couple of short hills, a week of easy running.
Full fitness and recovery around 2 months.
Returning too soon can manifest similarly to overtraining syndrome.
It is especially risky for athletes doing their first 100.
limitations: One coach's convention from an interview; no data cited; no per-distance figures for 50 km or 100 km. The page's illness details (cough, mononucleosis-like symptoms) were not re-confirmed and were dropped.
implications: A four-week staged return after a 100-mile race (rest, slow, slow with short hills, easy) is a comparator for the engine's 100-mile ramp, and about 2 months to full fitness.
Supports a more conservative return for first-time 100-milers; first-timer status is a plausible input if the engine has race-history data.

verification.notes: Re-fetched the page (WebFetch): page dated August 27, 2017 (year now confirmed); week structure, 2-month figure, overtraining resemblance and first-100 risk quotes present. Removed the earlier 'a week or two of solid running, then lethargy, illness' detail, which the fetch did not confirm. Practice source (programme, coaching or clinical page): a published convention, not evidence; grade D.

interests: David Roche sells coaching (SWAP) and a book; Andrew Skurka, who interviews him and publishes the page, is his coaching client.

r1.note: The four-segment month (rest, slow running, slow running with hills, easy running), 'around a full month', full fitness and recovery around two months, the overtraining-like return and the first-100 risk located in the Q&A on the page fetched 2026-10-31 (published 2017-08-27, modified 2019-10-16).

r2.note: The claims are David Roche's (the record's author). Human Kinetics' author page for The Happy Runner (read 2026-10-31) states that he started the SWAP coaching team in 2013, that athletes he coaches have won Western States and Hardrock, and that he is a two-time national champion. The interviewer is his client. Interests recorded.

r3.note: Interview of 2017-08-27 (modified 2019-10-16), read live. Later corpus papers (hoffman-2017, garciavaliente-2026) describe recovery of function over days to weeks and do not supersede a monthly staging.

r4.note: A staged month agrees in shape with Koop (cts-2025) and Powell (irunfar-2016) and with function data in millet-2011 and hoffman-2017. Roche's complete-rest week is shorter than Uhan's ten days (irunfar-2014); the conservative reading is the longer.

r5.note: Population is coach guidance for athletes recovering from a 100-mile race, mostly well trained; macroDesign.postRaceLongFractions and the H12 Params apply it to races of 100K and longer, labelled as defaults.

r6.note: Evidence level D, at the practice cap.
